items.stem: A formula that worked yesterday now shows #SPILL!. The most likely cause is:

options.text: A cell in the spill output range now contains data blocking the spill
options.rationale: Correct: #SPILL! appears when the cells a dynamic array needs to fill are not empty.

options.text: The function name was deleted from Excel
options.rationale: Built-in functions are not deleted; #SPILL! is a range-blocking error.
Theming does not cause spill errors.

items.explanation: Correct: #SPILL! appears when the cells a dynamic array needs to fill are not empty.

items.stem: Which TWO functions return a dynamic (spilled) array? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: FILTER returns all matching rows as a spilled array.
Correct: UNIQUE returns the distinct values as a spilled array.

options.text: A plain SUM of one range
options.rationale: SUM returns a single scalar, not a spilled array.
Number formatting is not a function and returns nothing.

items.explanation: Correct: FILTER returns all matching rows as a spilled array.

items.stem: XLOOKUP is preferred over VLOOKUP mainly because it:

options.text: Can look left or right and takes an explicit not-found argument
options.rationale: Correct: XLOOKUP is direction-independent and lets you set the value returned when nothing matches.

options.text: Automatically formats the result as currency
Creates a chart from the result
options.rationale: It returns a value, not a chart.

options.text: Requires the lookup column to be sorted
options.rationale: XLOOKUP does not require sorted data for an exact match.

items.explanation: Correct: XLOOKUP is direction-independent and lets you set the value returned when nothing matches.
